verses.verse:
स्वरालापाल्लयालापो मुक्तान स्ततो भवेत्।
गीतादिषु समायुज्य तान्स्तालेन समभ्यसेत्।१२६।
verses.text: From svarālāpa comes layālāpa, and from that the mukta tāna; joining these into songs and the like, one should practise them with the tāla.

commentary.text: Just as a bale of cotton is spread out and opened up, then given the form of thread and then made into cloth, after which the cloth is cut, sewn and so on according to one's various needs, and only then becomes fit for use - raw cotton by itself is used in only a few places - in the same way the ārohāvaroha (ascent and descent) form of a rāga is elaborated by the method of nyāsa and the rest, and then laya (tempo) is brought into that svara vistāra (elaboration of notes); this is called layālāpa (ālāpa in rhythm) or joḍ-ālāpa. Then, from it, on the basis of layakārī (rhythmic play) and the elements of tāna (tāna tattva), thread in the form of tānas is made. After that we are able to use them within a fixed tāla (metric cycle), together with tihāīs and so on. This is the meaning of the śloka above. As an example, three things are being presented in one rāga.
